issues.problem: R1-01/R1-03 class still open: many no-file, one-line reshapings of a delivery command get tier none, possible none, status ok, and completion-audit allows them silently. Root causes in the analyzer: (a) executed code it cannot see is not counted as possible delivery: "$@" and "${a[@]}"/${a[*]} expand to ONE field (Env.get joins positional with spaces), a dynamic command word with no visible args ("$(…)", "${a[@]}"), eval / sh -c of non-literal text, bash -s ARG (stdin code ignored, ARG treated as a script), bash /dev/stdin, . /dev/stdin, bash <(…), source <(…), python3 /dev/stdin, awk system() and sed e (code never scanned with _CODE_DELIVERY), script -qc, IFS-based splitting; (b) static_output models printf/echo -e escapes wrongly and returns a wrong literal instead of None ('\x67it' stays '\x67it'); (c) h_git/h_gh return None as soon as -h/--help appears anywhere, although git and gh take it as an option value (git commit -m --help, gh pr create --title -h); (d) git merge -n is treated as --no-commit (it is --no-stat); (e) git-<sub> binaries (/usr/lib/git-core/git-push, "$(git --exec-path)"/git-push) are unknown programs; (f) the walker gives up at MAX_DEPTH without any possible action (eval x30); (g) bash expansion-time execution is not modelled: arithmetic/subscript evaluation of literal variables ((( x )), [[ $x -eq 0 ]], let, $((x)), printf -v 'a[$(…)]', read 'a[$(…)]', [[ -v 'a[$(…)]' ]], ${!n}), ${x@P}, declare -a "a=($x)"; (h) parser divergence: coproc NAME { … } parses status ok as program NAME.

issues.suggested_fix: Treat anything executed that cannot be resolved as possible delivery (strictest tier), instead of none: dynamic command words with or without args, non-literal eval/sh -c/source/trap code, shells or interpreters reading /dev/stdin, /dev/fd/*, /proc/self/fd/* or process substitution, bash -s (always read stdin), awk system()/print|, sed e/s///e, script -c, depth/size limits. Expand "$@"/"${a[@]}" to separate fields (track arrays and positional lists), honour IFS assignments (or make unquoted expansions dynamic after IFS changes), return None from static_output for any escape it does not model (\x, \0NNN, \NNN, \u, \c, %b). Remove the global --help short-circuit (only skip when -h/--help is the first argument after the subcommand and not an option value). Fix git merge -n. Map basename git-<sub> to git <sub>. Walk literal values used in arithmetic/subscript contexts, ${x@P} and compound declare strings as code, or mark them possible delivery when they contain $( or a backquote. Parse coproc NAME compound. Add every shape above to the corpus as a gated case.

issues.problem: The agent can deliberately make the analyzer exceed the 15 s hook timeout or crash, and both fail open on the core gate. Work is exponential: each literal for-loop value re-walks the body (nested loops multiply), and each function call re-walks the body (a chain of functions each calling the next twice is 2^n). GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=99999999 loops 10^8 times; {1..30000000} builds a 30M-element list before the MAX_EXPANSIONS check; GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=² passes str.isdigit() and int() raises ValueError, so load-command prints no __end__ and classify.sh falls back to the regex tier, which misses obfuscated verbs. The base regex classifier had bounded cost, so this is a regression introduced by the fix (hooks.json gives completion-audit and dev-cycle-check timeout=15).

issues.suggested_fix: Give the walker a global work budget (nodes visited / commands executed / expansions, plus a wall-clock budget well under the hook timeout) and, when it is exhausted, stop and report the strictest possible tier (opaque reason 'analysis budget exceeded'). Do not re-walk loop bodies per value beyond a small product cap (walk once with the variable dynamic instead), memoise function bodies per (name, args) or walk them once. Bound GIT_CONFIG_COUNT (e.g. <= 64, parse with re.fullmatch('[0-9]{1,3}')), check the sequence length arithmetically before building it, and wrap analyze in a catch-all that returns status parse_failed with possible completion instead of crashing. Add tests for each (time limit + gated result).

issues.problem: classify.sh (F2-owned) does not fail closed on parse_failed, helper_unavailable or opaque executed code; it only adds a plain-verb regex over the text. FIX-BRIEF requires core gates to fail closed on unparseable input. Bash accepts several constructs the parser rejects, so an obfuscated verb after them is never classified; and opaque=false for executed script files and literal interpreter code, contrary to the schema doc ('true when some part cannot be resolved statically'), so a consumer that adopts 'fail closed on opaque' would still miss bash x.sh / . x.sh / python3 x.py. Honest commands almost never hit parse_failed (0 of 70 tricky-but-valid constructs in tools/syntax.py, 0 of 174 in tools/honest.py), so failing closed on it is cheap.
